fatal_errors: Element substitution does not independently vary atomic-size mismatch; it also changes bonding, elastic constants, valence-electron concentration, short-range order, stacking-fault energy, and phase stability, so the proposed comparison cannot uniquely attribute strengthening to lattice distortion.

The hypothesis does not reconstruct the target powder-processing route, nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structure, or the combined grain-boundary, dislocation-density, and solid-solution strengthening mechanism.
No cited or measured evidence is supplied to establish that the proposed alloys remain single-phase with matched grain size, texture, dislocation density, and porosity.
explanation: The response addresses the general question and offers a testable alternative centered on atomic-size-mismatch strengthening. Its single-phase and room-temperature boundaries are sensible, and it supplies a baseline, predicted direction, and nominal falsification rule. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target: it replaces HEBM plus SPS of CoCrFeNiTi with casting, rolling, annealing, and compositional substitution; omits the specified processing window; and misses the target's nanocrystalline 83% FCC/17% BCC mediator and synergistic Hall–Petch, dislocation, and solid-solution mechanisms. It also provides no quantitative predictions corresponding to approximately 675 Hv and 1894 MPa. Scientifically, the experiment is only moderately discriminating because changing an element alters many variables besides atomic radius, while HRTEM alone is insufficient to isolate a bulk lattice-distortion metric. Stronger support would require matched grain size, phase fraction, texture, porosity, and dislocation density, together with quantitative local-structure measurements such as total-scattering/PDF or EXAFS and strength correlations across several independently designed compositions.
